summary.text: Heather Baxter is the Republican nominee for South Dakota secretary of state. A Rapid City small-business owner who represents District 34 in the state House, she won the nomination at the party convention after losing her own House primary.
She is running on election integrity, including hand-counted paper ballots and stronger audits.

paragraphs.text: Baxter describes herself as a lifelong South Dakotan and a small-business owner in Rapid City and Custer.
She has also worked as a strength and flexibility coach for older adults.
She has served on the Pennington County Republican executive board and says she has volunteered at local shelters, her children's schools and a church childcare ministry.
Baxter was elected to the South Dakota House in November 2024 and represents District 34 in Pennington County.
She announced her candidacy for secretary of state in September 2025, when she was challenging incumbent Monae Johnson.
She lost her June 2, 2026, Republican primary for re-election to the House, but won the secretary of state nomination at the Republican convention, defeating Johnson.
Baxter supports hand-counted paper ballots and improved audits, and she co-sponsored a bill to prohibit automatic tabulating machines.
She says that as secretary of state she would work with county auditors rather than eliminate the machines on her own.

Her campaign site says only 4 of South Dakota's 66 counties can fully audit elections through cast vote records and promises to give every county the audit tools and training, to enforce the state's proof-of-citizenship laws, and to pursue campaign finance reporting reform and an "SD DOGE" to cut regulation for small businesses.
